metadata.title: Veil — Passkey-Powered Stellar Wallets

register.title: Register
register.body: Your browser creates a P-256 key pair. The public key goes on-chain. The private key never leaves your device.

approve.title: Approve
approve.body: A biometric prompt — Face ID, fingerprint, Windows Hello — signs the Soroban auth payload. No password. No phrase.

verified.title: Verified
verified.body: The Soroban contract verifies your P-256 ECDSA signature on-chain. Trustless. Invisible. Done.

noSeedPhrases.title: No Seed Phrases
noSeedPhrases.body: Nothing to write down, nothing to lose. Your biometric is the only key you need.

noExtensions.title: No Browser Extensions
noExtensions.body: Works in any modern browser. No installs, no plugins, no platform lock-in.

accountAbstraction.title: Account Abstraction
accountAbstraction.body: Soroban custom accounts unlock gas sponsorship, multi-sig, and social recovery — built-in.

devQuickstart.description: The Veil SDK wraps the full WebAuthn + Soroban pipeline into a single React hook. Register a passkey wallet, sign auth entries, and recover accounts — without touching a private key.

ecosystem.description: Veil wallets are Soroban custom account contracts — a native Stellar primitive. Each transaction settles with Stellar finality: sub-cent fees, 3–5 second confirmation, and the full security of the Stellar network backing every signature.

trust.label: Security
trust.title: You should not have to trust us. So we built it so you don’t have to.

items.title: Non-custodial by construction
items.body: Your wallet is a contract only your passkey can authorise. Veil cannot move your money, freeze it, or sign on your behalf — there is no key on our side to do it with.

items.title: Builds you can verify
items.body: The contracts are compiled reproducibly in a pinned container. The bytecode running on Stellar mainnet matches our published hashes byte for byte, and you can rebuild it yourself to check.

items.title: A published threat model
items.body: We wrote down how Veil could be attacked, using STRIDE, and shipped it in the docs rather than keeping it internal. Known limitations are listed alongside the mitigations.

items.title: Open source, MIT
items.body: The wallet, the contracts, the oracle and the indexer are all public and permissively licensed. Nothing about how your money moves is hidden from you.

items.q: Do I need to know anything about crypto?
items.a: No. You sign in with your face or fingerprint, and your balance is shown in your own currency. There is no seed phrase to write down, no gas token to buy, and no wallet address to memorise before you can be paid.

Yes, and provably. Your funds sit in a smart contract that only your passkey can authorise. Veil holds no key that can move them, so there is nothing for us to freeze, lend out or lose. The trade-off is real: self-custody means no support line can reverse a transaction you signed.

items.q: What happens if I lose my phone?
items.a: Your passkey lives in your device’s keychain and, for most people, syncs through Apple or Google. Signing in on a new device uses that same passkey. Keep a copy of your wallet address somewhere outside the app — recovery is fastest when you have it.

Nothing to open, and network fees are sponsored, so a transfer costs you zero. Stellar itself charges a fraction of a cent, which Veil covers. Where a third party is involved — a swap venue, an anchor — their fee is shown before you sign, never after.

items.q: Where does the yield come from?
items.a: From Blend, a lending pool on Stellar: your USDC is borrowed by others who post collateral, and they pay interest. It is not a Veil product and not a guaranteed rate. It is DeFi, the rate moves, and pools carry smart-contract risk. Nothing is deposited unless you approve it with your passkey.

items.q: Is this actually live, or a prototype?
items.a: Live on Stellar mainnet. The contracts are deployed and source-verified, and the core flows have real transactions behind them — a passkey-authorised spend and a live DEX swap among them. Bills and airtime are the exception: those need a licensed partner in each market and are not switched on yet.

agent.body: Ask in plain words and the agent builds the transaction — a swap, a transfer, a recurring bill. It hands you an unsigned payload every time. Your passkey is the only thing that can send it.
